pierhead_guide.text: Welcome to the Pierhead Building. It went up in 1897 for the Bute Dock Company, in red terracotta that glows at sunset.
The style is French Gothic, and the clock tower looks like a cousin of Big Ben who has been on holiday in France.
Next door is the Senedd, the Welsh Parliament building, all glass and slate, opened in 2006. It was made to be see-through on purpose.

then.text: Pop next door to the Senedd some time. The public gallery is free, and the debates come in two languages.

else.text: Shwmae! I do the tours next door at the Senedd, the Welsh Parliament. It's had a few names, so bear with me.
In 1997 Wales voted on having its own assembly. Yes won by 50.3%, fewer than seven thousand votes in it. My taid still says he swung it.
The National Assembly for Wales was first elected in May 1999. It won full law-making powers in a 2011 referendum, and since 2020 it's been the Senedd.
It makes the laws on health, schools, farming, transport and the Welsh language. Defence, foreign affairs and most taxes stay with Westminster.
Members speak Welsh or English, with live translation. So you can hear a row about bus timetables in two languages at once.
Noted in the Gazetteer, under How these isles work.
